attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The 'as AI contributes' clause is his assertion, even though it sits inside a recommendation.

semantics.note: The causal clause is stated firmly and is separate from the 'should be watching' advice, which is not graded. The proposition matches his words.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: AI raises perpetrators' scale or output, without being the sole cause. Counting more output as escalation is a fair reading of the word, but it decides the result because the evidence on reach is weak.

evidence.note: FBI release dated 2024-05-08, inside the period. It says AI increases attack scale and that criminals increasingly use voice and video cloning for fraud. This covers the fraud half and names a mechanism.

OpenAI first-party threat report, May 2024. It says five influence operations produced content in greater volume with AI, but saw no meaningful gain in reach. This is a company disclosure. It supports more output, not more impact.

reviews.rationale: Both parts are supported within the 2024 period. The FBI documents AI adding scale and impersonation ability to fraud. OpenAI's threat report documents AI raising disinformation output. The weak reach in e2 limits the impact finding, but under the contract more output counts as escalation.

attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I will be surprised if' states a firm expectation that neither candidate will say much and neither will commit, so it is scored. The drafter's 'likely' wording is a little softer than his words, but the content is the same.

contract.note: Treating a passing mention as consistent with 'not much' is a fair, ordinary reading of 'much of anything'. Requiring a concrete action against a named AI harm is a fair test of a commitment.

evidence.note: The transcript shows the Harris–Trump debate took place on 2024-09-10. This establishes the event, not what was said about AI.
Transcript shows Harris mentioned AI once, in passing, about winning the technology race. Trump answered about chips. Neither made an AI-harm commitment.

reviews.rationale: The debate took place on the forecast date. The only AI reference was Harris's brief remark about winning the race on AI. Nobody discussed AI policy in substance, and neither candidate committed to reducing any AI harm. Both predicted absences held.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. He asserts 'growing problem' himself inside the recommendation.

semantics.note: The revised proposition keeps only the growth assertion and correctly drops the hedged clause about teenage girls.

contract.note: Reading 'growing' as more incidents or more circulation is ordinary. Using the 2024 period with earlier comparison years is reasonable.

evidence.note: Korean National Police release dated 2024-08-27. Synthetic sexual image cases went from 156 to 160 to 180 a year (2021–2023), then 297 in January–July 2024. Police describe the threat as sharply rising.
IWF measured a fall in AI child-abuse images on one dark-web forum. That is a different, broader category and one site only. It qualifies the picture but does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Korean police data show recorded cases of nonconsensual sexual deepfakes in the first seven months of 2024 well above any full earlier year. The IWF decline is for a different measure on one forum. Police counts cannot separate more offending from more reporting, but they show a growing problem as the speaker described it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own closing sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The antecedent 'if we don't let them know' is kept. 'Certainly' makes the forecast firm but it is largely rhetorical. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Requiring evidence that the antecedent held before scoring is fair. The contract does not add a deadline the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: January 2024 poll shows public concern about AI. It does not show what any candidate was told.
CAIP scorecard and advocacy show some voters were urged to contact candidates. It does not establish whether the antecedent held or failed for any candidate.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The evidence does not show whether citizens failed to tell any identified candidate that AI policy matters, so the antecedent is unknown and the claim cannot be scored. No conclusive event exists.
